newsitem.title: USA: Paxson buys ITT/Dow Jones TV station, to launch network.
newsitem.headline: Paxson buys ITT/Dow Jones TV station, to launch network.

text.p: Paxson Communications Corp. said Monday it agreed to acquire WBIS Channel 31 in New York City from a partnership of Dow Jones Inc. and ITT Corp. in a deal valued at $257.5 million.
Paxson said the channel, its 50th, will become the flagship station of the West Palm Beach, Fla.-based company's proposed new nationwide broadcast TV network.
In a joint statement, the sellers said they made a gain on their investment in the station, which they bought from the City of New York in 1996 for $207 million.
The deal is part of ITT's effort to sell non-core assets and focus on its hotel and gambling operations as it fends off a $6.5 billion hostile takeover bid by Hilton.

Dow Jones is tightening operations as it tries to appease shareholders' demands that it sell Dow Jones Markets, formerly Telerate, the New York-based company's financial news and information unit which has lagged behind rivals Reuters Holdings Plc and Bloomberg LP.
Paxson said it is the largest U.S. TV station broadcaster, owning, operating or with affiliates covering more than 57 percent of all U.S. TV households.

In the run-up to the launch of the new network later this year, the station -- to be renamed WPXN TV-31 -- will sell air time to ethnic, foreign language, religious, cable and speciality programmers as well as infomercial entrepreneurs.

Paxson, which also owns 43 radio stations and 507 billboards throughout Florida, said it will operate the station under a time brokerage agreement from June 30 until the deal closes in the fourth quarter.
Dow Jones is expected to terminate its business news as of June 29.

Paxson Chief Executive Lowell Paxson told reporters the station would continue to carry the 21 hours a week of sporting events and news provided by Liberty/Fox Sports -- a venture of News Corp. Ltd. and Liberty Media Corp.
The deal is subject to regulatory approval, which is expected later this year. It is not subject to financing conditions, the companies said.
With the sale of its stake in the station, New York-based ITT still has a handful of valuable assets to divest, including businesses in international telephone directories and educational services.
Paxson's stock fell 37.5 cents to $10 on the American Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading. ITT was unchanged at $59.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.
